title: Alan Turing Way mine shaft: shored excavation and drilling platform as temporary works
excerpt: Ground Engineering (20 November 2026) reports Manchester City Council’s response to a March 2026 depression on Alan Turing Way that revealed an unrecorded 3 m diameter, 50 m deep mine shaft. Investigation used a 6.4 m × 6.3 m shored excavation and a drilling platform constructed over it. More than 100 t of grout and a 550 mm reinforced concrete cap followed. For contractors these are temporary works items: excavation support, plant platforms over voids, buried services interfaces and load-path verification under BS 5975-1:2024 and CDM 2015.
linkedinReady:
A shored excavation and a drilling platform over an unrecorded mine shaft are temporary works, not just investigation logistics.

Ground Engineering reported on 20 November 2026 that Manchester City Council closed the northbound carriageway of Alan Turing Way after a depression appeared in late March. Specialist investigations identified an unrecorded historical mine shaft approximately 3 m in diameter extending to 50 m below ground level, with workings at about 40 m. The initial investigation used a shored excavation roughly 6.4 m by 6.3 m through soft made ground to about 6 m. Ground investigation and treatment were complicated by United Utilities and Openreach apparatus crossing the hole. Probe drilling was carried out from a drilling platform constructed over the excavation.

Stabilisation (mid-September to early October) placed more than 100 t of grout into the shaft and surrounding ground, with loose backfill to the top of the glacial till and a 550 mm reinforced concrete cap. Foam concrete and stone then reinstated levels in the initial excavation.

Contractors should treat the shored excavation, the platform over the void, and the service crossings as temporary works under the project procedure and BS 5975-1:2024. That means a design brief covering ground conditions, plant loads, surcharge, buried services, exclusion zones and the residual risk of further collapse until the permanent cap and reinstatement are complete. A highway reopening decision does not replace a competent temporary works inspection or permit.

Educational briefing only. Not for construction.

body.p: Ground Engineering published on 20 November 2026 an account of Manchester City Council’s works on Alan Turing Way. A depression in the road surface in late March 2026 led to closure of the northbound carriageway between Ashton Old Road and Grey Mare Lane. Initial speculation of a utility failure was superseded by specialist investigations that identified an unrecorded historical mine shaft. A Manchester City Council spokesperson told GE that the area was investigated through a shored excavation approximately 6.4 m by 6.3 m in extent, with soft made ground recorded to about 6 m below ground level. A smaller area of around 3 m by 2 m immediately beneath the initial feature contained a greater thickness of made ground. Ground investigation and treatment works were complicated by the depth of the excavation and by United Utilities and Openreach infrastructure across the hole. Ground investigation was completed in the surrounding area and from a drilling platform constructed over the excavation. Rotary percussive probe holes, including inclined probes, from that platform identified an approximately 3 m diameter mine shaft extending to 50 m below ground level, with mine workings at about 40 m. The Mining Remediation Authority completed desktop research on 1 June 2026 and determined the issue was not coal-mining related. Stabilisation work between 17 September and early October pumped more than 100 t of grout into the shaft and surrounding ground, added loose shaft backfill to the level of the top of the glacial till, and installed a 550 mm thick reinforced concrete cap over the shaft. Foam concrete and stone reinstated levels within the initial excavation. Road reconstruction is expected to allow reopening by early to mid-December.

The shored excavation and the drilling platform constructed over it are temporary works. They support plant, people and investigation loads above and beside an unrecorded deep void in soft made ground, with live utility apparatus crossing the works. Until the permanent cap and reinstatement are complete and accepted, residual risk of further ground movement or collapse remains. CDM 2015 Regulation 19 requires that a structure be stable and capable of withstanding the loads to which it is subjected during construction. BS 5975-1:2024 sets out the management procedures (register, design brief, design check, TWC/TWS roles, permits) that demonstrate those duties are being met for temporary works. A public-highway interface and buried services raise the consequence of failure. The fact that the Mining Remediation Authority concluded the feature was not coal-mining related does not remove the need for a temporary works design brief that covers the actual ground conditions, the platform loading, the shoring system and the sequence of grouting and capping.

ul: Enter the shored excavation and the drilling platform as separate or linked items on the Temporary Works Register. Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure; escalate where deep voids, soft ground, live services or public interface are present.

Require a design brief that records excavation geometry, ground conditions (including soft made ground thickness), plant and surcharge loads on the platform, buried services clearances, exclusion zones and the residual risk until the permanent cap is in place and verified.
Verify the load path for the drilling platform: how loads are transferred into competent ground or supported across the excavation without relying on the void or unpropped soft ground.

Coordinate with utility owners (United Utilities, Openreach) for temporary support, protection or diversion of apparatus crossing the excavation. Do not treat service crossings as outside the temporary works scope.
Inspect shoring and the platform after any change in ground conditions, rainfall, or additional plant. Do not reuse an earlier inspection once the sequence has moved to grouting or capping.
Do not proceed with excavation, platform loading, grouting or capping until the arrangement has been reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.
